title: memory-client.ts is a triple-dead client: spawns 'python3' (does not exist on Windows per the repo's own platform rule), imports scripts.agentica.memory_factory (absent from the repo), and its only consumer (skill-usage.ts) is referenced by zero hooks

evidence.quote:
from scripts.agentica.memory_factory import create_default_memory_service
        memory = create_default_memory_service(session_id)
Windows does not have `python3` on PATH. The `python3` command triggers the Microsoft Store alias and fails.

observe_how: git ls-files shows the only memory_factory in the repo is opc/scripts/core/db/memory_factory.py — no scripts/agentica/ package exists anywhere, so the embedded import can never resolve even on a machine with python3. The 'graceful fallback' (return []/null on any error) masks the breakage completely. Grep across hooks/src excluding shared/ finds zero callers of trackUsage/recordSkillUsage/searchMemory/storeMemory; only shared/index.ts re-exports them. trackUsage+UsageRecord are also duplicated verbatim in both memory-client.ts (lines 379-455) and skill-usage.ts (92 lines) — dead weight twice over (~550 lines).

title: In-process embedding fallback (~30-45s cold load) can never complete inside the hook's 12s SIGKILL budget — when the daemon route fails Python-side after the TS probe passed, the recall burns 12s and returns nothing, losing even the FTS results

evidence.quote:
Pays the ~30s sentence-transformers import + bge-large load on first
    call within this process. Subsequent calls within the same process
    are fast.

# Prior value was 0.2 s. The TS hook correctly used 1500ms, but Python re-pinged
# at 200ms, slipping under load → fell to in-process embed → 12s SIGKILL.

observe_how: The 2026-05 fix widened the Python re-ping to 1.5s, but the structural TOCTOU remains: TS isDaemonReady can pass, then Python's daemon_is_alive/ping/embed (5s cap) can fail under load, routing to _embed_query_inproc whose cold sentence-transformers load (~30-45s per embedding_daemon.py docstring) is guaranteed to exceed the 12s spawnSync budget. The hook then records db_subprocess_timed_out=true and source='empty'. A budget-aware fallback (fail the embed and run FTS-only inside the same process, or an env kill-switch for in-proc embed when invoked from the hook) would convert these 12s/empty outcomes into ~1s text hits.
telemetry: memory-recall.jsonl db_subprocess_timed_out field; by_source empty=154/281 (55%) includes these SIGKILL outcomes.

title: Hybrid relevance gating is mathematically dead: effective threshold 0.002 is below the minimum possible top-pool RRF score (~0.0152), and the vector arm has no absolute-similarity cutoff — any query always yields k*2 'nearest' candidates

evidence.quote:
default=0.2,
        help="Minimum similarity threshold (default: 0.2, filters low-quality results)",

ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY embedding <=> ${embedding_param}::vector) as vec_rank
            FROM archival_memory
            WHERE {where_clause}
            AND embedding IS NOT NULL

observe_how: With rrf_k=60 and LIMIT k*2=6, the worst row in the returned pool scores at least 1/(60+6)=0.0152 whenever >=6 embedded rows exist (corpus has 100+), so the 0.2*0.01=0.002 filter can never remove anything — the help text's 'filters low-quality results' is false in the default mode. Because vec_rank is pure ROW_NUMBER over cosine distance with no cutoff, a nonsense query ranks the corpus identically to a good one; the only differences are which rows are 'nearest'. Consequence: the memory_recall_relevance Braintrust score (topScoreRaw) measures rank arithmetic + age, not semantic relevance — it is decision-risky to tune floors against it.
telemetry: top_score p25/p50=0, p75=0.0149 — the distribution is bimodal empty-vs-0.015, exactly what rank-only scoring predicts.

title: Awaited Braintrust HTTP emit (≤2s) in the recall hot path on EVERY user prompt, fired after total_elapsed_ms is captured — user-perceived latency is under-reported by the hook's own telemetry
observe_how: New instance of the SEED-16 pattern (sync bounded HTTP in a hot path), but on the RECALL side which fires on every qualifying user prompt (281 logged rows), not just stores. total_elapsed_ms is computed at line 610 before the emit at ~659, so the 13-17s telemetry already excludes up to 2 more seconds of awaited POST. Note the emit-invariant guard (audit-braintrust-emits.sh) requires the await — any fix must move the emit off the prompt path (e.g. detached child), not just drop the await.
telemetry: Compare wall-clock prompt-to-injection time vs memory-recall.jsonl total_elapsed_ms.

title: correlation_id is structurally inert: no hook emitter sets it, the facade's per-call randomUUID appears in exactly one row, and backfill hardcodes null — root cause of corr-null 60.7%

evidence.quote:
/** Correlation id tying related events together. */
  correlation_id?: string;

observe_how: In .claude/logs/intel-bus.jsonl (647 rows at review time): only the 125 facade rows (find-symbol/who-calls/rename-preview/bus/code-context/recall) carry a non-null correlation_id; all hook rows (bus_write 158, agent_recall_bus_read 48, memory_awareness_bus_read 42, bus_read_latency 34, bus_write_dropped 14) omit the field; 226 backfilled rows carry explicit null. Each facade UUID appears exactly once (one appendIntelRow per main() invocation at scripts/code-intel.mjs:1098), and parent_event_id is never set anywhere — so even non-null ids correlate nothing.
telemetry: harvest SUMMARY corr-null 60.7% on 318 live rows; live file now 647 rows with 125 non-null UUIDs (80.7% null-or-absent)
causal_links: D4a-03 (the offline downstream_used / proposal-application analysis the schema anticipates needs correlation, which cannot work today)
SEED-10 (C.3 telemetry watch would consume this field)

title: intel-bus redaction escapes: quoted secret values containing spaces leak their tail, and common key shapes (Google AIza..., github_pat_..., glpat-..., Azure AccountKey=, PASSPHRASE=) pass both the shape pass and the keyword pass

evidence.quote:
.replace(/sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,512}/g, 'sk-[REDACTED]') // OpenAI
    .replace(/AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}/g, '[REDACTED-AWS-KEY]') // AWS access key id
    .replace(/gh[posru]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,255}/g, '[REDACTED-GH-TOKEN]') // GitHub
    .replace(/xox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,512}/gi, '[REDACTED-SLACK-TOKEN]') // Slack

observe_how: Concrete escapes from reading the regexes: (1) PASSWORD="my secret pass" — ASSIGNMENT_RE value class [^\s]{1,2048} stops at the first space, redacting only `"my` and leaving `secret pass"` in clear; (2) bare Google API keys (AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}) match no standalone shape; (3) GitHub fine-grained github_pat_... is not covered by gh[posru]_; (4) GitLab glpat-... absent; (5) Azure storage `AccountKey=...` — 'AccountKey' matches neither SECRET_KEY_RE nor the anchored SECRET_FIELD_NAME_RE (no bare KEY alternative); (6) PASSPHRASE= matches no keyword. Defense-in-depth context: events are allowlist-constructed, so exposure requires a free-text field (e.g. a focus term or future caller) carrying one of these shapes.
telemetry: no leaked-secret rows observed in the live log; gap is latent
causal_links: D4a-06 (the duplicated mjs appender has NO redaction at all, widening this gap for any future free-text field)

title: bus-tool-populator writes the bus on EVERY Read and Grep, but the ambient (grep_hit) slice it populates has no behavioral consumer — recall readers use load_bearing/focus_symbols only — so each Grep pays a node spawn + lock + full JSON rewrite for display-only data and amplifies the contention behind the 158 slow / 14 dropped writes

evidence.quote:
*   - Grep  -> files_in_play role `grep_hit` (AMBIENT -- a softer signal; the 30% ambient cap
 *              in addFileInPlay keeps grep noise from flooding out load-bearing context).

observe_how: extractBusFocus (the ONLY recall-bias reader, shared by memory-awareness and agent-recall-injector) reads focus_symbols + files_in_play.load_bearing and never touches ambient; the sole ambient consumer is the on-demand `/code-intel bus` display (21 invocations in the live log). Meanwhile every Grep PostToolUse spawns bus-tool-populator, scans up to 200 response lines with realpathSync/statSync per candidate, then takes the bus lock and rewrites the whole context.json. Telemetry: 158 bus_write rows crossed the 50ms slow threshold (write_ms up to 2362) and 14 writes dropped. Either give ambient a reader (it was designed as recall signal) or gate/batch the Grep-path writes.
telemetry: intel-bus query_type counts: bus_write 158, bus_write_dropped 14, bus_read_latency 34; `bus` display calls 21
causal_links: D4a-02 (these per-tool writes are the contention source for the leaky-cap waits and drops)
